newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends barely up before USDA estimate.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends barely up before USDA estimate.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed slightly firmer after retracing early losses amid speculative buying that emerged just before the close, dealers said.
Activity remained rangebound as many players stood on the sidelines ahead of Monday's USDA report.
USDA will issue its final planted area estimate for the 1997/98 cotton crop at 0830 EDT.

Expectations for fewer planted acres than the 14.485 million estimated in March, have contributed to recent gains. An estimate below 14.0 million, however, is expected to trigger further speculative buying, lifting the December contract over resistance seen at 77.70 to 77.95 cents a lb.
Market Analysts have pegged USDA's number between 13.83-14.30 million acres.
Benchmark December delivery settled 0.24 cent higher at 77.40 cents, traded 77.44 to 76.93 cents, with the rest 0.20 higher to 0.05 weaker.
An estimated 14,000 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Thursday's official 13,009 lots.
